per_question.question: How do I reset my password?
per_question.answer:
The process for resetting your password depends on your account type:

* For standard accounts: Navigate to Settings, select Security, and then choose Reset Password. You will need to enter your account's email address to receive a reset link, which remains valid for 24 hours. If your account is currently locked due to 5 failed login attempts, you can still request this link to unlock your account immediately.
* For SSO (Single Sign-On) accounts: There is no in-app password reset option. Because your credentials are managed by your organization's identity provider, you must contact your IT administrator to reset your password directly through them. The standard consumer reset flow will not affect your SSO login.
* For accounts transitioning from SSO: If your organization disables SSO, you will revert to a standard login. If you never previously set a password, you must use the "forgot password" flow to establish one.
per_question.reference_answer: Go to Settings, then Security, then Reset Password. Enter your account email and a reset link will be sent; the link expires 24 hours after it's issued.

per_question.question: What are the password requirements?
per_question.answer:
For accounts that utilize standard email and password authentication, passwords must meet the following criteria:

* Length: They must be at least 10 characters long.
* Complexity: They must include at least one number and one symbol.
* History: They cannot match any of the user's previous five passwords.
per_question.reference_answer: Passwords must be at least 10 characters long and include one number and one symbol. A new password cannot match any of the last 5 passwords used.
per_question.llm_judge_reasoning: The candidate answer includes all the same requirements: minimum length of 10, at least one number and one symbol, and no reuse of the last five passwords.

per_question.question: How does SSO login work for enterprise accounts?
per_question.answer: For organizations on the Enterprise plan, SSO login functions as a mandatory authentication method that replaces the standard email and password login screen. Once an account owner enables SSO via the Organization Settings, all members are required to authenticate through their chosen identity provider, such as Okta, Azure AD, or Google Workspace [1, 2]. Because the standard login screen is disabled, users do not use the platform's consumer password reset flow; instead, they must follow the specific SSO and Enterprise Login procedures [4]. Additionally, two-factor authentication for these accounts is managed entirely through the identity provider's settings rather than the platform's internal 2FA flow [3].
per_question.reference_answer: Organizations on the Enterprise plan can enable SSO through an identity provider such as Okta, Azure AD, or Google Workspace. Once enabled, all members must log in through the identity provider's page instead of the standard email/password screen.

Because SSO accounts are managed entirely by your organization's identity provider rather than the platform, the standard consumer password reset flow is disabled and will not affect your SSO login. If you are unable to log in, you must contact your organization's IT administrator to have your credentials reset directly within the identity provider.

per_question.question: How do I set up two-factor authentication?
per_question.answer: The method for setting up two-factor authentication (2FA) depends on whether your organization uses enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO). For standard accounts, you can enable 2FA by navigating to Settings, then Security, and selecting Two-Factor Authentication. You will need to scan the provided QR code using an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy and enter the 6-digit code from the app to confirm the setup. Once enabled, you will be provided with 10 single-use backup codes that should be stored securely in case you lose access to your authenticator app. However, if your organization uses enterprise SSO, you do not use this in-app flow; instead, 2FA is managed directly through your identity provider's own settings.

per_question.question: What happens when I exceed the API rate limit?
per_question.answer: When you exceed the API rate limit, the system returns a 429 status code to indicate that the request was unsuccessful. To help you manage this, the response includes a `Retry-After` header, which specifies the number of seconds you must wait before attempting your next request. Additionally, if you continue to receive 429 errors within a short timeframe, the system may impose a temporary IP-level throttle on top of the existing account-level limit.
